subject: Extracting M N-vectors from N-array of M-vectors

messages.author: a2d460b4e88b69d8
messages.subject: Extracting M N-vectors from N-array of M-vectors
parts:
Hi all,

if I have an N-array of say 2 vectors that is sampled from a multivariate normal in a vectorized way:
vector[2] y[N];
...
y ~ multi_normal(mu_y,Sigma_y);

Can I extract two vectors of length N y1 and y2 (to work with them in the generated quantities block) without giving up the vectorized sampling of y? I can see that this might be possible with the head or segment functions, but I am not sure.

Thanks,
Thomas

messages.author: a2d460b4e88b69d8
messages.subject: Re: Extracting M N-vectors from N-array of M-vectors
parts:
I meanwhile tried
y1 <- to_matrix(y)'[1];
but this throws an error suggesting that arg 0 type=vector[1].
According to the manual 2-d arrays can be used as argument to to_matrix?

Thanks,
Thomas

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Extracting M N-vectors from N-array of M-vectors
parts:
In generated quantities, you should do something like the following:

generated quantities {
  matrix[2,N] y_matrix;

  for(n in 1:N)
   col(y_matrix,n) <- y[n];

...
...
}


Rob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Extracting M N-vectors from N-array of M-vectors
parts:
Does anyone have suggestions on how to make these
messages clearer? I'm taking a pass through errors now
and this particular one seems to confuse a lot of our
users.

The problem you're having is that you're passing an
array of vectors to to_matrix(). The only valid arguments
are either a matrix, a vector, a row vector, a 2D array
of real or a 2D array of int. An array of vectors doesn't
match any of those.

For a start, I think I'll replace "vector[1]" with just
"vector[]". That will at least make the type print out match
the way way types are defined in functions. I think vector[1]
is confusing with the declaration. So "int[2]" would look
like "int[,]".

- Bob
